chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from al-Nakha'i from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'A man forgot throwing the Jamarat.' He said, 'He returns and throws them.' I said, 'If he forgot them until he arrived in Mecca?' He said, 'He returns and throws them separately, and separates between each two throws by an hour.' I said, 'If he forgot or was unaware until it passed and he left?' He said, 'There is no obligation upon him to repeat it.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: His saying 'There is no obligation upon him to repeat it' means he is not obligated to repeat it in this year, although repeating it may be obligatory upon him in the coming year, either by himself if able, or by ordering someone to act on his behalf. And this is because the days of throwing are the days of Tashriq; so if they pass him, nothing is obligatory upon him except in the coming year during similar days.

key_terms.أَيَّامُ التَّشْرِيقِ: Days of Tashriq (the days of throwing Jamarat)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim forgets to throw the Jamarat stones during Hajj?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, highlighting the juristic distinction between forgetting the Jamarat throws before departing Mecca versus after the days of Tashriq have elapsed. Imam al-Sadiq clarifies that if the pilgrim leaves without throwing, the obligation is not immediate but deferred to the following year, either performed personally or through a proxy, reflecting the principle that the specific temporal window for this act has closed.
